# eBird/Avonet
```{r loading in ebird and avonet data from files}
# cran release
require(tidycensus)
require(data.table)
require(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tictoc)
library(auk)
library(janitor)

# Getting started with loading in the CA ebird data and filtering later

# Stage 1: Setting the working directory and pathway for the files
# set the directory for the location where the data is saved 
# raw files are listed below
base_dir <- "/Users/tyusdwilliams/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats"
combined_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_v11")
f_ebd_filt <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_filtered_v11.txt")
f_smp_filt <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_filtered_sampling_v11.txt")

if(!file.exists(f_ebd_filt)){
  # Alameda
  dir_001   <- file.path(base_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_smp_relSep-2025")
  f_ebd_001 <- file.path(dir_001, "ebd_US-CA-001_smp_relSep-2025.txt")
  f_smp_001 <- file.path(dir_001, "ebd_US-CA-001_smp_relSep-2025_sampling.txt")
  
  # Contra Costa
  dir_013   <- file.path(base_dir, "ebd_US-CA-013_smp_relSep-2025")
  f_ebd_013 <- file.path(dir_013, "ebd_US-CA-013_smp_relSep-2025.txt")
  f_smp_013 <- file.path(dir_013, "ebd_US-CA-013_smp_relSep-2025_sampling.txt")
  
  ## ============================================================
  ## 2. Helper to combine eBird txt files WITHOUT breaking format
  ## ============================================================
  
  # This keeps file1 exactly as-is (comments + header + data),
  # and appends only data rows (no comments/header) from file2.
  combine_ebird_txt <- function(file1, file2, outfile) {
    # read all lines of file1
    lines1 <- readLines(file1)
    
    # read all lines of file2
    lines2 <- readLines(file2)
    
    # find first non-comment line in file2 (the header row)
    header_idx2 <- which(!startsWith(lines2, "#"))[1]
    
    if (is.na(header_idx2)) {
      stop("Could not find header in second file: ", file2)
    }
    if (header_idx2 >= length(lines2)) {
      stop("No data rows found in second file: ", file2)
    }
    
    # data rows start AFTER the header
    data2 <- lines2[(header_idx2 + 1):length(lines2)]
    
    # write all of file1 + data rows from file2
    all_out <- c(lines1, data2)
    writeLines(all_out, outfile)
    
    invisible(outfile)
  }
  
  ## ============================================================
  ## 3. Create merged East Bay EBD + sampling files
  ## ============================================================
  
  # combined_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_v11")
  dir.create(combined_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  f_ebd_merged <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_v11.txt")
  f_smp_merged <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_sampling_v11.txt")
  
  # IMPORTANT: this overwrites any broken merged files you created earlier
  combine_ebird_txt(f_ebd_001, f_ebd_013, f_ebd_merged)
  combine_ebird_txt(f_smp_001, f_smp_013, f_smp_merged)

  
  f_ebd_merged <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_v11.txt")
  f_smp_merged <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_sampling_v11.txt")
  
  
  ## ============================================================
  ## 4. Set up auk with the merged files
  ## ============================================================
  
  ebd_auk <- auk_ebd(f_ebd_merged, file_sampling = f_smp_merged)
  
  # Example filters: complete checklists + standard protocols
  ebd_auk_filt <- ebd_auk |>
    auk_complete() |>
    auk_protocol(c("Stationary", "Traveling", "Area"))
  # you can add more filters here:
  # |> auk_year(2000:2025) # what is the range of years? Should we filter the years?
  # |> auk_bbox(c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax))
  
  ## ============================================================
  ## 5. Apply filters on disk and read back in
  ## ============================================================
  
  # Output filtered files
  f_ebd_filt <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_filtered_v11.txt")
  f_smp_filt <- file.path(combined_dir, "ebd_US-CA-001_013_smp_relSep-2025_filtered_sampling_v11.txt")
  
  auk_filter(
    ebd_auk_filt,
    file          = f_ebd_filt,
    file_sampling = f_smp_filt,
    overwrite     = TRUE
  )
  
}

sampling_full <- read_sampling(f_smp_year_filt)

# since the files are in a spec_tbl_df format we need to convert to df

# attach the avonet traits before you manually zerofill
# Load Avonet info to join with the bird data
avonet_trait = read.csv('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/ELEData/TraitData/AVONET1_BirdLife.csv') %>% 
  dplyr::select(Species1, Family1, Order1, Wing.Length, Kipps.Distance, 
         Mass, Mass.Source, Habitat, Migration, Habitat.Density, Trophic.Level,
         Trophic.Niche, Primary.Lifestyle, Range.Size) %>% 
  mutate(scientific_name = Species1) # subset the AVONET file for desired traits

# Step 1: Join AVONET info with the ebird observations
# How many mismatched species for checklists
mismatch_species_checklist = unique(ebd_2020$scientific_name[! ebd_2020$scientific_name %in% avonet_trait$scientific_name])

# How many mismatches are there?
mismatch_species_checklist # there are 28 mismatched species

ebd_2020$scientific_name == avonet_trait$scientific_name # check if this matches now, this seems to be right

ebd_traits <- ebd_2020 %>%
 left_join(avonet_trait, by = "scientific_name") #Ensure scientific names match
ebd_dt <- as.data.table(ebd_traits)

fwrite(
  ebd_dt,
  file = "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/data/ebd_with_avonet.txt",
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  na = "",
  row.names = FALSE
  )

# Now we join the adjusted names and summarize the checklists
ebd_summary <- ebd_traits %>% 
  group_by(checklist_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(observation_date, latitude, longitude)) %>% 
  summarize(
    # Count the total unique species in general
    total_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name),
    # Count unique species for each category
    # 3 & 2 = Migratory/Partial and 1 = Resident
    migrant_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name[Migration %in% c(2, 3)]),
    resident_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name[Migration == 1]),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
    glimpse()

# now set the observation count to numeric and find missing rows
ebd_2020 <- ebd_2020 %>%
  mutate(
    # Replace "X" with "1" before coercion
    observation_count = if_else(observation_count == "X", "1", observation_count),
    observation_count = as.numeric(observation_count))
ebd_2020$observation_count <- as.numeric(ebd_2020$observation_count) # X DOES NOT MEAN ABSENCE!
# NAs introduced by coercion here
# This is because they used to be an "X" to denote that a species was observed but the quantity was unknown.

# Step 3: Join the sampling events (The Zero-Fill)
# This ensures that checklists where NO migrants/residents were seen get a 0.
ebd_complete_zf <- sampling_subset %>%
  left_join(ebd_summary, by = "checklist_id") %>%
  mutate(
    # Replace NAs from the join with 0 to represent true non-detections
    migrant_richness = replace_na(migrant_richness, 0),
    resident_richness = replace_na(resident_richness, 0),
    # Optional: A simple flag and logic column if any bird was seen
    species_observed = (migrant_richness + resident_richness) > 0)

# relocate the columns of interest in the new zerofilled dataset now
ebd_complete_zf <- ebd_complete_zf %>%
  relocate(c(checklist_id, migrant_richness, resident_richness,
             species_observed), .before = last_edited_date) %>% 
    dplyr::select(-v34) # remove this column

# How many resident/migrant observations are there?
# Migratory observations total
sum(ebd_complete_zf$migrant_richness) # 2.3 millions observations
# Resident observations total
sum(ebd_complete_zf$resident_richness) # 1.1 million observations
```

# Reproj Vars
```{r filtering the predictor variables to the spatial extent of the block group}
# pull the needed covariates of interest to the block group in my study area
# covariates include: noise, light, income, ndvi, migration_mean, temp, rain
# elevation, impervious surface area, % of landcover, housing/population density
here::i_am("cat_bird_chapter.Rmd")
setwd("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats")

# using the same variables as before
# list the variables of interest that I want to use
acs_vars = c(medincome = "B19013_001", total_income = "B19001_001", pop = "B01003_001", housing = "B25001_001")

# Grab the California boundary + centroid in lon/lat
ca <- tigris::states(year = 2022) |>
  filter(NAME == "California") |>
  st_transform(4326)
ca_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(ca))
lon0 <- ca_centroid[1]
lat0 <- ca_centroid[2]

laea_ca <- paste0(
  "+proj=laea ",
  " +lat_0=", lat0,
  " +lon_0=", lon0,
  " +x_0=0 +y_0=0 ",
  " +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
)

bg_covs <- get_acs(
  geography = "block group",
  variables = acs_vars,
  state     = "CA",
  county    = c("Alameda", "Contra Costa"),
  year      = 2024,
  geometry  = TRUE
) |>
  # wide: one row per block group
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols   = c(GEOID, NAME, geometry),
    names_from  = variable,
    values_from = estimate
  ) |>
  # project to CA-centered LAEA for area calc
  st_transform(laea_ca) |>
  mutate(
    area_km2        = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6,
    pop_density     = pop / area_km2,
    housing_density = housing / area_km2
  ) |>
  # back to WGS84 for eBird points / auk
  st_transform(4326)

# fix the arrangement of the sf table now
bg_covs <- bg_covs %>%
  relocate(area_km2, .after = geometry) %>%
  relocate(pop_density, .after = pop) %>% 
  relocate(housing_density, .after = housing) %>% 
  relocate(c(housing_density, housing), .after = pop_density) %>%
  mutate(across(c('area_km2', 'pop_density', 'housing_density'), \(x) round(x, digits = 2)))

# now we turn the block group area into a vector format to interpolate the covariates
bg_v <- vect(bg_covs)

# --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Spring Migration:
# --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# raster extract the spring migration layer into the eb_outline or census block group geometry
spring_migrate <- rast('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/GIS_data/spring_stopover_2500_v9.tif')
bg_v_crs <- project(bg_v, spring_migrate)
spring_migrate_crop <- crop(spring_migrate, bg_v_crs)
spring_migrate_mask <- mask(spring_migrate_crop, bg_v_crs)
spring_migrate_mask_trim <- trim(spring_migrate_mask)  # removes outer NA borders

wgs84 <- "EPSG:4326"
spring_migrate_mask_trim_crop <- project(
  spring_migrate_mask_trim,
  wgs84
  # method = "near"  # categorical raster (impervious % / classes)
)
dir.create('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars')
writeRaster(
  spring_migrate_mask_trim_crop,
  "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/spring_stopover_2500_v9_clip_wgs84.tif",
  overwrite = TRUE
) # spits out the new spatial raster layer for the reprojected variable

# remove the SpatRaster layers from the workspace because you no longer need them
rm(spring_migrate, spring_migrate_crop, spring_migrate_mask, spring_migrate_mask_trim, spring_migrate_mask_trim_crop)

# --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
ALAN = rast("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/GIS_data/EastBay_2020_2024_nightlights.tif")
bg_v_crs <- project(bg_v, ALAN)
ALAN_crop <- crop(ALAN, bg_v_crs)
ALAN_mask <- mask(ALAN_crop, bg_v_crs)
ALAN_mask_trim <- trim(ALAN_mask)  # removes outer NA borders

wgs84 <- "EPSG:4326"
ALAN_mask_trim_crop <- project(
  ALAN_mask_trim,
  wgs84
  # method = "near"  # categorical raster (impervious % / classes)
)

writeRaster(
  ALAN_mask_trim_crop,
  "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/ALAN_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84.tif",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# remove the spatraster files that we dont need
rm(ALAN, ALAN_crop, ALAN_mask, ALAN_mask_trim, ALAN_mask_trim_crop)

#--- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# Traffic Volume Rasterization
#--- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- ---
# 1. Load ALAN raster (Template)
ALAN_template <- rast("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/ALAN_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84.tif")

# 2. First pull in the calenviroscreen data and select for traffic volume
calenviro_traffic <- st_read("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/eb_shapefiles/calenviroscreen.v4/CES4 Final Shapefile.shp") %>% dplyr::select("Traffic")

# 3. Clean + prep the vector
calenviro_traffic <- st_transform(calenviro_traffic, crs = crs(ALAN_template))
traffic_v <- vect(calenviro_traffic)

# Need to fix the min value so the map visuals are better
# Replace placeholders with real NA values
traffic_v$Traffic[traffic_v$Traffic < 0 ]  <- NA

# 4. Crop vector to study area
# Convert ALAN raster extent to vector for cropping
study_area_vect <- as.polygons(ext(ALAN_template), crs = crs(ALAN_template))

traffic_v_subset <- crop(traffic_v, study_area_vect)

# -------------------------------
# 5. Rasterize using ALAN as template
# -------------------------------
traffic_raster <- terra::rasterize(
  traffic_v_subset,
  ALAN_template,
  field = "Traffic",
  fun = "mean"
)

# -------------------------------
# 6. Clean raster
# -------------------------------
traffic_raster_trim <- trim(traffic_raster)

# -------------------------------
# 7. Quick sanity checks
# -------------------------------
print(minmax(traffic_raster_trim))
hist(traffic_raster_trim)
summary(traffic_raster_trim)

plot(traffic_raster_trim, main = "Traffic Volume Raster")
plot(study_area_vect, add = TRUE)

# -------------------------------
# 8. Save (already in WGS84)
# -------------------------------
writeRaster(
  traffic_raster_trim,
  "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/traffic_volume_final_wgs84.tif",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# -------------------------------
# 9. Cleanup
# -------------------------------
rm(calenviro_traffic,
  traffic_v,
  traffic_v_subset,
  traffic_raster,
  traffic_raster_trim,
  study_area_vect, ALAN_template)
```

```{r creating sf buffer points and extracting covariates}
library(tmap)

### Pulling the census data and getting area based interpolations ###

# now we need to load in the socioeconomic data for the counties concerning our sites for Alameda and Contra Costa
# first lets looks the variables from ACS
vars23 <- load_variables(2020, "acs5")

View(vars23) # this will show us the census table data

# list the variables of interest that I want to use
acs_vars = c(medincome = "B19013_001", total_income = "B19001_001", pop = "B01003_001", housing = "B25001_001")

# Grab the California boundary + centroid in lon/lat
ca <- tigris::states(year = 2022) |>
  filter(NAME == "California") |>
  st_transform(4326)
ca_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(ca))
lon0 <- ca_centroid[1]
lat0 <- ca_centroid[2]

laea_ca <- paste0(
  "+proj=laea ",
  " +lat_0=", lat0,
  " +lon_0=", lon0,
  " +x_0=0 +y_0=0 ",
  " +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
)

bg_covs <- get_acs(
  geography = "block group",
  variables = acs_vars,
  state     = "CA",
  county    = c("Alameda", "Contra Costa"),
  year      = 2024,
  geometry  = TRUE
) |>
  # wide: one row per block group
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols   = c(GEOID, NAME, geometry),
    names_from  = variable,
    values_from = estimate
  ) |>
  # project to CA-centered LAEA for area calc
  st_transform(laea_ca) |>
  mutate(
    area_km2        = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6,
    pop_density     = pop / area_km2,
    housing_density = housing / area_km2
  ) |>
  # back to WGS84 for eBird points / auk
  st_transform(4326)

# double check the missing values of the dataframe
bg_diag <- get_acs(
  geography = "block_group",
  variables = acs_vars,
  state = "CA",
  county = c("Alameda", "Contra Costa"),
  year = 2024,
  survey = "acs5",
  geometry = FALSE,
  output = "wide"
) %>% 
  mutate(
    county = case_when(
      str_detect(NAME, "Alameda County") ~ "Alameda",
      str_detect(NAME, "Contra Costa County") ~ "Contra Costa",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    income_is_na = is.na(medincomeE),
    households_zero_or_na = is.na(housingE) |
      housingE == 0,
    pop_zero_or_na = is.na(popE) |
      popE == 0
  )

# spit out table for the diagnostic really quick as well
bg_diag %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarise(
    n_block_groups = n(),
    n_income_na = sum(income_is_na),
    pct_income_na = mean(income_is_na) * 100,
    n_income_na_and_no_houses = sum(income_is_na & households_zero_or_na),
    n_income_na_with_households = sum(income_is_na & ! households_zero_or_na),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# check the sum of the missing values
table(is.na(bg_diag$medincomeE))

 # fix the arrangement of the sf table now

  relocate(pop_density, .after = pop) %>%

  mutate(across(c('area_km2', 'pop_density', 'housing_density'), \(x) round(x, digits = 2)))

# now we turn the block group area into a vector file to interpolate the covariates
bg_v <- vect(bg_covs)

temp = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'bio1_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
precip = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'bio12_mask_trim_crop_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
elevation = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'elev_mask_trim_crop_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
ndvi = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'ndvi_mask_trim_crop_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
imp_surf = rast("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/nlcd_impervious_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84.tif") # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
nlcd_landcover = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'nlcd_landcover_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
spring_migration = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'spring_stopover_2500_v9_clip_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
ALAN = rast(list.files('~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2aviancats/reprojected_vars/', full.names = T, pattern = 'ALAN_mask_trim_crop_clip_wgs84')) # Load all .tif, not geodatabase
```

```{r making various maps representing eBird data in the East Bay}
# 3.0 million or 3,047,888 for total observations made

# building out a table for the summary statistics ebird data
list(colnames(bg_covs_ua))

# lets make the same summary statistics table for chapter 2
# lets pull the variables we need
variable_pull <- colnames(bg_covs_ua[c(17:23,30)])
variable_pull <- variable_pull[c(-9)]
# Function to compute stats for a single variable
get_stats <- function(x) {
  c(
    total  = sum(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean   = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    min    = min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Apply the function to each variable
ebird_summary_stats <- bg_covs_ua %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(variable_pull)) %>%
  map_df(get_stats, .id = "variable") %>%
```

## Trait Grab
```{r join avian traits and summarize with habitat types}
# Note: Now we are interested in pulling the specific functional diversity traits for chapter 3 in this section.
# Step 1: check the state of the dataset and make sure the info is accurate
# see if you can do this use the raw base R
ebd_w_traits$year <- lubridate::year(ebd_w_traits$observation_date)

table(lubridate::year(ebd_w_traits$observation_date)) # okay we do have 2022 and 2023 data

# Step 1: First, we need to filter the data to our range of interest
# Create a NEW object so we don't overwrite the original 'ebd_w_traits'
ebd_22_23 <- ebd_w_traits %>%
  mutate(obs_year = year(observation_date)) %>% # Create a explicit year column
  filter(obs_year %in% c(2022, 2023))

# double check the table to see the range again
table(lubridate::year(ebd_22_23$observation_date)) # this worked

# Step 2: CALCULATING HABITAT PERCENTAGES/COUNTS
## Based on lifestyle and habitat association ##
#### Create new cols for habitat percentage/counts types ####
# Step 1: create column for forest, urban, aquatic, and understory. Might change later
ebd_22_23$habitat_type <- dplyr::case_when(ebd_22_23$Habitat %in% c("Forest", "Woodland") ~ "forest",
  ebd_22_23$Habitat %in% c("Shrubland", "Grassland") ~ "understory",
  ebd_22_23$Habitat == "Human Modified" ~ "urban", ebd_22_23$Habitat %in% c("Wetland", "Coastal", "Marine", "Riverine") ~ "aquatic", TRUE ~ "other") # this works, updated 04/03/2026

# double check the format really quick
glimpse(ebd_22_23$habitat_type)

# Step 3: Estimating the migratory and resident richness by habitat types for chapter 3
ebd_habitat_summary <- ebd_22_23 %>%
  group_by(habitat_type) %>%
  summarize(
    # Total unique species in this habitat
  total_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name),
  
  # Break it down by your Chapter 3 categories
  migrant_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name[Migration %in% c(2, 3)]),
  resident_richness = n_distinct(scientific_name[Migration == 1]),
  
  # Optional: Count how many checklists were submitted in each habitat
  # This helps you see if one habitat looks "richer" just because it has more data
  n_checklists = n_distinct(checklist_id),
  .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Calculate the richness per checklist to control for effort
  mutate(richness_per_effort = total_richness / n_checklists) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_richness))

# Take a look at the results
print(ebd_habitat_summary) # this would make a great table for the paper

# make csv file for chapter 3 paper
write.csv(ebd_habitat_summary, file = "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch3urbancat_eBirdtrends/ch3_habitat_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# csv was written 04/03/2026

# Step 4: Creating cols for habitats and grouping by checklists for chapter 3
checklist_habitat_counts <- ebd_22_23 %>% 
  group_by(checklist_id, habitat_type) %>% 
  summarise(species_count = n_distinct(scientific_name), .groups = "drop") 
# this looks right for now

# check the format
glimpse(checklist_habitat_counts)

# Step 5: Now we need to pivot the table wider and grab the columns
habitat_count_wide <- checklist_habitat_counts %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(checklist_id), names_from = habitat_type, values_from = species_count) # then join this with the ebird summary data and get the coords
# do not fill missing slots with NA values
# check the format for accuracy
print(habitat_count_wide) # looks good
# perfect this worked, each row should have a count for each habitat type

# Step 6: Now we bind the pivoted habitat counts with ebird summary
# then we join the lat/long and observation counts from ebd_22_23
ch3_ebd_habitat <- ebd_summary %>%
  left_join(habitat_count_wide, by = "checklist_id") %>%
  relocate(c(forest, understory, urban), .before = aquatic) %>% 
  glimpse() # now that this is done grab info from ebd_22_23 and join

# Select lat/long and observation counts and join using checklist_id
ebd_22_23_subset <- ebd_22_23 %>%
  distinct(checklist_id, latitude, longitude) %>%
  dplyr::select(checklist_id, latitude, longitude) %>%
  glimpse() # grab the coords
# now we can join the info based on the matching checklist_id column
ch3_ebd_habitat <- ch3_ebd_habitat %>% 
  left_join(ebd_22_23_subset, by = "checklist_id") %>% 
  relocate(c(latitude, longitude), .after = checklist_id) %>% 
  glimpse() # this should work and then turn it into gpkg for chapter 3 pull

summary(ch3_ebd_habitat) # lots of missing values

ebd_habitat_omit <- na.omit(ch3_ebd_habitat) # just for a clean version

# now we save the file as a gpkg format to use in chapter 3
ebd_habitat_omit <- st_as_sf(ebd_habitat_omit, coords = c("latitude", "longitude"),
                            crs = 4326) # 4326 is the standard WGS84 (lat/long)
st_write(ebd_habitat_omit, "~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch3urbancat_eBirdtrends/ch3_ebd_habitat.gpkg")
# this should now give us the habitat type data we need for chapter 3 manuscript

# make sure to remove data frames you no longer need!
rm(ebd_summary, ebd_habitat_summary, checklist_habitat_counts, habitat_count_wide, ebd_22_23, ebd_22_23_subset, ch3_ebd_habitat)

```

## Glm Models
```{r visualizing and modeling the data from ebird pres_absence dataset}
### Consider I will have three major models relating to my questions ###
# 1) The luxury effect of digital data:
# Number of complete checklists ~ Anthropogenic + Environmental + Climatic Variables
# 2) The luxury effect and bird biodiversity patterns:
# Number of bird species ~ Anthropogenic + Environmental + Climatic Variables
# 3) The luxury effect and functional diversity:
# Migratory density ~ Anthropogenic + Environmental + Climatic Variables
# Percentage of forest taxa (or grassland specialists) ~ Anthropogenic + Enviro + Climate

### Example of model types below ###

# 1) Data model [N.obvs ~ anthro vars + enviro vars + climate vars]
# 2) Biodiversity model [N.species & Migration ~ anthro + enviro + climtate]
# 3) Func Traits model [ % forest, % urban, & % understory ~ anthro + enviro + climate]

### Predictor variables of interest ###
# median income, housing density, ndvi, migration density, temp mean, light pollution, and noise pollution/traffic volume

# check the missing data values of the dataset before you run the models

# make sure the data is loaded in for the models

bg_covs_ua <- st_read("~/Desktop/Meso_Study/ch2_ebird_eastbay/Output/bg_covs_urban_only_all_socioeco_ebird_anno.gpkg") # great this worked and it's in WGS 84 CRS format

# run a correlation matrix to look at the relationship between vars!! ##
variables <- bg_covs_ua %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(4, 8, 18:26) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), scale)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) # using this for the matrix table

cor.matrix <- cor(variables, use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# make the matrix plot
corrplot::corrplot(cor.matrix, method = "square", 
                   type = "full",
                   addCoef.col = "black",
                   addCoefasPercent = FALSE,
                   outline = TRUE,
                   insig = "pch",
                   p.mat = NULL,
                   tl.col = "black",
                   tl.srt = 45) # this looks fine will improve later

# final variables: ALAN, traffic_volume, housing density, income, and temperature

# Try looking at GAM w/ GLMM outputs or using lm/lme4 #
# load in the dredge package and see all the possibilities with covs
# first we need a clean dataset, make df out of the urban block group
list(colnames(urban_scaled))

urban_scaled <- bg_covs_ua %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(c(4:9,24:29,31,32), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
 # should be better now

# test the correlation between my predictor variables
# Check correlations between your predictors
cor(urban_scaled[, c("housing_density", "traffic_volume", "ALAN", "medincome", "precip", "temp", "ndvi")], use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# we need to make sure the cbg data columns are in the integer format
glimpse(urban_scaled)
urban_scaled$cbg_n_records <- as.integer(urban_scaled$cbg_n_records)

# set area_km2/checklist density as a log version and see how the models run

resident_model <- glmmTMB(cbg_resident_richness ~ traffic_volume + 
ALAN + medincome + precip + offset(log_areakm2), 
data = urban_scaled, family = nbinom2(link = "log")) # nbinom2 is Negative Binomial
```

## Fig Plots
```{r visualizing the models through tables and figures}
### EXTRACTING PLOTS FOR MODEL FOR PAPER ###
# Now we need to find a way to pull the plot images from our sjPlot predictive function

# 1. Put your models in a named list and organize vars along with colors
model_list <- list(
  "Resident Diversity" = resident_model,
  "Migrant Diversity" = migratory_model,
  "eBird Checklists" = checklist_model,
  "Radar Stopover" = radar_stopover_model)

predictors <- c("housing_density", "traffic_volume", "ALAN", "medincome", "precip", "temp")

quad_colors <- c("red3", "royalblue", "forestgreen", "purple3")

# 2. Outer loop: Iterate through each predictor variable
  for(var in predictors) {

# 3. Use a inner loop to generate a list of plots for each model for the current predictor
# Replace terms section with the actual predictor variables we want to plot
plot_list <- lapply(seq_along(model_list), function(i) {
  m_name <- names(model_list)[i]
  m_color <- quad_colors[i] # this picks the colors in order for each section
  
    p <- sjPlot::plot_model(model_list[[m_name]],
                       type = "pred",
                       terms = var, # Do NOT include the offset term here
                       colors = m_color, # sets the line/ribbon color now
                      title = paste(m_name)) + # Adds model name as the title/facet header
    sjPlot::theme_sjplot() +
      # Bold axes and increase the font sizes for publication
      theme(
        axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"), # Bold x & y titles
           axis.text = element_text(size = 13),  # Bold axis numbers
           plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")  # Bold plot headers
         )
    
    # FIX: if plot_model returns a list, just take the first element
    if(is.list(p) && !inherits(p, "ggplot")) p <- p[[1]]
    return(p)
})

# 3. Combine the 4 model plots into one 2x2 grid for this predictor
combined_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list, ncol = 2) # 2x2 grid is the visual

# 4. Save each grid as its own file
ggplot2::ggsave(filename = file.path(output_folder, paste0("Supplemental_Grid_", var, ".jpg")),
          plot = combined_plot,
          width = 15,
          height = 10,
          dpi = 500)
  } # we will pdfs of these in the future for the publication/supplemental files

print(combined_plot) # quick preview of the plot output

 ## Model Output Table ##

# first we list the models with their respective names

   "Resident Diversity" = resident_model,
   "Migrant Diversity" = migratory_model,

   "Radar Stopover" = radar_stopover_model)
 
 # now we try to create a succint table using model summary
 ch2modeltable <- modelsummary::modelsummary(model_list,
                            fmt = 2,
                            estimate = "{estimate} [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                            statistic = c("s.e. = {std.error}",
                                          "z = {statistic}",
                                          "p = {p.value}"),
                            metrics = c("AIC","F","RMSE"),
                            coef_omit = "Intercept",
                            stars = FALSE,
                            output = "tinytable")
 # looks good! Now save this.
 
 # double check the table and make sure it looks fine
 ch2modeltable
 
 # save the tinytable file dataset into my github page
 tinytable::save_tt(ch2modeltable,

# now we make the plot for the 95% coefficient plots, looks great!
```
